decision: counted the work before starting, four workstreams: the sync lever, the skill sync, the extension, the docs
why: a long run needs a size and a checkable finish line before the first commit
result: frame set

decision: built verify-sync.mjs first and captured the pre-change baseline
why: so the check reads as old value against new value instead of an opinion
evidence: scripts/verify-sync.mjs, baseline 113 unexplained of 141 upstream files
result: baseline recorded

decision: declared every Pi adaptation as data in pi-deltas.json, with a rule that matches nothing failing the run
why: hand re-application is why the port sat at upstream 0.14.4 while upstream reached 0.15.2
result: 43 rule-explained deltas, 0 unexplained, reruns idempotent

decision: used whole-file overrides with a baselined upstream hash for the three files we rewrite
why: rules could not express a rewrite, and a silent revert of our stronger version was the risk being fixed
result: an upstream edit to those files now fails the check

decision: vendored upstream pstack 0.15.2 through the lever
why: eight releases of drift had accumulated
result: PASS, 0 unexplained, 0 stale rules

decision: adopted upstream's forge-neutral shipping instead of requiring Graphite
why: a reader without Graphite was blocked, and the fix was free by vendoring
result: shipping lands through gh or origin

decision: kept our stronger opening non-negotiable in the mode skill and baselined the file as an override
why: upstream's density pass deleted the instruction to read the Principles first while its own guide diagram still shows that step
result: instruction preserved, upstream edits still detected

decision: widened the port lint after it missed real Cursor coupling in shipping.md
why: a lint that misses cases is worse than none, because it certifies a false clean
result: coupling and long-dash checks both fail the build now

decision: corrected the prompt-cost figure from 371 to 402 tokens and disclosed that upstream hides how, why, unslop, and typescript-best-practices
why: a fresh-context check measured the real tree and disagreed with my first number
result: corrected, consequence documented for the user

decision: reframed the competitor's skill-strip as a runtime toggle rather than a feature we judged worthless
why: their port deletes upstream's flags, so both designs land in the same default state and the toggle is the real difference
result: candid difference stated, mechanism trade documented

decision: made the port lint fail on the long-dash character, not just on Cursor coupling
why: the package teaches that the character is banned, so shipping it in its own skills contradicts the rule
result: 0 long-dash characters across skills, agents, and docs

decision: removed the usage-doc headers from our two shipped Node scripts and kept only the non-obvious why comments
why: the no-comments rule applies to files this package ships, and the playbook already documents what each script does
result: both scripts still run

decision: caught the command-substitution rule rewriting link targets and breaking a guide link
why: the rule matched /setup-pstack inside skills/setup-pstack/SKILL.md, so a command rename silently corrupted a path
result: rule narrowed with a lookbehind, link check added to the lint

decision: removed the host model slugs the light tier wrote and replaced them with inherit plus thinking levels
why: a published package was writing opencode-go/hy3 and a deepseek fallback into a stranger's settings
result: tier pins no model, test fails if a slug reappears

decision: reported the prompt cost in /pstack-status instead of building a skill-hiding feature
why: the number is what decides the comparison, and hiding skills is the competitor's approach rather than a measurement
result: status line prints the live figure

decision: fixed a pre-existing bug where the -l fast path wrote to the user settings file
why: the parsed scope value project was tested with startsWith against the picker's capital-P label, so it fell through to user
result: '-l writes .pi/settings.json

decision: re-measured the delegate's token figure myself and found my own 367 was an invocation error
why: a relative skills path shortens the location field, so the estimate dropped by 35 tokens
evidence: extensions/skill-budget.ts with an absolute skills dir
result: 402 confirmed against the live TUI capture

decision: recorded that a harness run wrote the light tier into the real user settings and the subagents block was restored by hand
why: no pre-incident copy of that block exists to diff against, so the restore cannot be independently confirmed
evidence: ~/.pi/agent/settings.json, backups/ holds only an Aug 26 copy with no subagents key
result: residual risk reported, recovery is /pstack-setup inherit

decision: mutation-tested the parity check itself instead of asserting it works
why: a fresh-context reviewer could not test anything, so the guard needed a committed artifact proving it catches real defects
result: 5 of 5 mutations caught, tree unchanged after

decision: recorded that the first review attempt could not run anything
why: the reviewer agent ships read, grep, find, and ls only, so a brief that asks for tests gets static analysis instead
result: retrying the gate with an agent that has bash

decision: caught the port up with two upstream commits (#365 slug retune, #366 budget ask) and shipped the Pi-harness feature set: budget tiers, context guard, poteto compaction, doctor, playbook completions
why: both ports with this name ship the same skill list, so the durable difference has to be what the harness can do that a skill cannot; upstream's budget ask maps one-to-one onto Pi's thinking ladder

decision: ported upstream's budget ask as subagents.defaultThinking instead of a new private key, and derived the recorded budget label from that key on re-runs
why: upstream records a "# budget:" line in its own rule file; Pi already has a native key for the same concept, and a derived label means no schema to migrate
result: unlimited clears the key instead of writing a value

decision: loaded the conversation serializers through a guarded dynamic import rather than a static one
why: peerDependenciesMeta marks pi-coding-agent optional, so a static runtime import could fail to resolve on installs where the host package is not reachable from this package's node_modules chain
evidence: compaction.ts loadConversationHelpers; the import is dynamic, the CompactionResult type import is erased at compile time
result: unresolved helpers degrade to Pi's default compaction, never a failed extension load

decision: the poteto compaction path is typechecked, unit-tested against fakes, and smoke-tested for module resolution, but not exercised against a live provider mid-run
why: no provider key is wired into the verification environment, and faking a full compaction would test the fake
evidence: buildSummaryPrompt and runPotetoCompaction tests, pi -e RPC smoke test
result: fallback to default compaction covers every failure path
